engineering_checks.name: constructor_and_inherited_lifecycle
engineering_checks.assessment: The constructor requires E0RelativeIdentity, constructs the protected Tracker directly and installs the existing M1 guard with commit_guard=True. It does not invoke the legacy epoch9 checkpoint constructor or instantiate a three-input identity head. The supplied relative head is moved to the model parameter device, put in eval mode and frozen. Tracker construction puts the model in eval mode; M1 guard construction wraps model.predict. Inherited set_sequence retains positive-valid-frame stride25 sampling. Initialization first clears/disables guard observation, then initializes base state, creates the original two-encoder anchor and clones fixed initial templates; the override resets relative diagnostics. Inherited close restores the original predictor.
engineering_checks.independent_evidence: The actual constructor and inherited initialize/set_sequence/close executed with synthetic CPU model outputs and scoped CUDA boundary substitutions. A trap confirmed the legacy constructor was never called. Reinitialization cleared prior sequence state and observation records, ran exactly two anchor encoders and made zero predictor calls. The fixed templates were an independent clone, and close restored the saved bound predictor.

engineering_checks.name: causal_M1_gate_and_existing_cadence
engineering_checks.assessment: The previous position is copied before guard.track. The guarded E0 call advances the frame once, updates ordinary query/history state and computes M1 from that same prediction. Recovery eligibility uses that resulting frame and predicted m1_state==2, with no label, extra threshold or new sampling rule. Non-lost sampled frames and lost unsampled frames return the guarded box and route without current/candidate encoding or relative-head inference.
engineering_checks.independent_evidence: State0/frame1, state1/frame1 and state2/frame2 each executed one original predictor and zero recovery encoders; relative-head hooks were set to fail on an unexpected invocation. The guard's reliable/uncertain/lost template-write behavior was also exercised on frame5.

engineering_checks.name: current_proposal_feature_binding_and_no_future_labels
engineering_checks.assessment: Current evidence uses the current image cropped about the preceding position, factor4 and size256; its ROI is the guarded current E0 output box transformed from image xywh into this crop's normalized cxcywh coordinates. Both modalities use fixed initial templates and return features[2,768]/coverage[2], then gain a batch dimension for the relative head. Candidate enumeration uses the same image, preceding position and fixed templates. This matches the full current-E0 collector's evidence convention. There is no current/future GT, label, IoU or benchmark metadata argument in the runtime decision path. An initial target box and caller-provided valid-frame cadence remain inherited inputs.
engineering_checks.independent_evidence: The actual current helper and candidate helper executed together on a synthetic image. Captured arguments confirmed preceding-state geometry, current returned box and the identical fixed-template object. Existing current-evidence CPU tests separately checked modality order, normalized geometry, read-only inputs and uncovered ROI behavior.

engineering_checks.name: five_input_actual_head_KEEP_masks_and_candidate_index
engineering_checks.assessment: The five positional inputs are anchor, current features, current coverage, candidate features and candidate coverage. E0RelativeIdentity prepends current E0 to the candidate evidence, removes the old scalar no_match output and gives action0 the explicit KEEP meaning. torch.argmax's first index preserves current E0 in an exact score tie. Current coverage with no fully observed modality forces score0=0 and all replacements=-inf; uncovered candidates are masked. Replacement index k maps to existing candidate box[k-1] without sorting or relabeling candidates.
engineering_checks.independent_evidence: An actual-head exact tie returned KEEP through the real helper chain. A real randomly initialized relative head, with explicit synthetic features chosen to make the final candidate score highest, selected index24 and committed box23 in all four action/modality combinations. Zero and fractional-only current coverage forced KEEP even with favorable candidates; all-uncovered candidates also returned KEEP. Old three-input heads, nonfinite features/coverage and inconsistent candidate-coverage shape were rejected. Existing actual-head tests verified scalar no_match independence.

engineering_checks.name: position_history_only_commit_and_M1_write_ownership
engineering_checks.assessment: KEEP returns the guarded output and retains its state/history. A replacement assigns only float32 position and the eight-element history: modality one-hot, original route confidence, normalized center displacement from the pre-track position, log size change and existing since_query/100. It does not advance frame, reset since_query, write or restore templates, or change route confidence/action/modality. M1 remains the owner of this frame's E0 template-write decision. Returning a replacement uses a position copy.
engineering_checks.independent_evidence: The independent harness executed the real Tracker and M1 guard. On a proposed frame5 write, reliable M1 allowed the write while uncertain/lost M1 restored only the dynamic template. Fixed initial templates stayed unchanged. For each action0/1 and modality0/1 replacement, actual-head selection of candidate24 matched the expected history; frame stayed1 and since_query stayed8 for action0 or0 for action1, with no M2 template write. Provided tests independently checked KEEP history identity and replacement state.

engineering_checks.name: encoder_accounting_and_external_timing_contract
engineering_checks.assessment: Successful recovery diagnostics record two current encoders and24 candidate encoders, matching two modalities for current evidence and12 dual-modal candidate queries. Non-recovery and initialization reset these per-track counters to0. They are additive recovery encoder counts, not total model work: initial anchor uses two encoders per sequence, M1 and the relative head have their own work, and the ordinary E0 computation is separate. The returned route.seconds still measures the base Tracker call and excludes later guard/current/candidate/head work. The explicit class contract therefore correctly requires external timing of the whole track call; a future entry must synchronize and account for whole initialization as well.
engineering_checks.independent_evidence: With actual current/candidate helpers and counted synthetic model encoders, one recovery track recorded exactly26 added encode calls and24 primary calls, alongside one original predictor. Initial anchor separately used two encoders. No production timing, FPS or measured GPU cost is established here.
